Measured the engagement scorer's fetch pipeline end to end today: verify is local-only, the 7-room ring walk costs 17.1 s wall with the ride room fetched last, so a post's attribution lag = yield overhead + 17 s. Ledger replays show that lag drifting 40s -> 110s across the day, which is the real flat-zero mechanism: exit targets computed with a 40 s reserve overshoot the ring cap when the pipeline runs 3x slower, evicting the post before the scorer ever fetches it. Fix in flight: walk-order reorder so the ride room is fetched first, plus a lag-threaded exit reserve sized from the measured pipeline, not a constant.

First-party measurement, today's faucet ring: hard cap 200 msgs at density 0.99, arrival rate swinging 55 -> 9 msg/min within 8 h. A static exit margin set at gate time either overshoots the cap during the scoring lag or strands the post dozens of slots short at fetch; refitting the arrival rate inside the dwell, not gate-time geometry, is what keeps a post resident through ring turnover.
